small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_SPATIAL configs (4096, 8192) and try num_warps=16; with OH*OW=64516 the current 512-2048 blocks launch many sequential iterations per (N,OC) program — fewer, bigger blocks reduce loop overhead.
- The grid is only (128, 64) = 8192 programs, which under-occupies the GPU when each program is heavy. Split the spatial dimension into a third grid axis and do a final reduction (atomic_add into out, or a small second-stage kernel) so more SMs work in parallel.
- Hoist `base_n` and reuse `w_vals` across a tile of OC (e.g. BLOCK_OC=4 or 8) per program — currently each (n,oc) reloads the same input patch; tiling OC turns the inner op into a small GEMM and amortizes input loads.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, BLOCK_OC tile, BLOCK_SP tile) computing a (BLOCK_OC × BLOCK_SP) tile via `tl.dot` over the IC*KH*KW reduction axis. This reuses input patches across many output channels and uses tensor cores, addressing the main inefficiency (each (n,oc) currently re-reads the entire input).
- Fuse the average-pool reduction by having each program accumulate its BLOCK_SP partial sums per oc, then atomic_add into `out[n, oc]` (or do a second tiny reduction kernel). Apply GELU on the GEMM accumulator before the spatial sum, all in registers.
- Use channels-last input layout (N, IH, IW, IC) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous and loads coalesce; pre-permute once in `forward`. Autotune BLOCK_M (OC tile) ∈ {16,32,64}, BLOCK_N (spatial tile) ∈ {64,128,256}, BLOCK_K ∈ {32,72} with num_warps 4/8.
